title: What changed in 2025 to 2026
summary: A dated map of the API, protocol and platform changes that break code or old advice, with GA, Preview, Deprecated or Retired status checked on 2026-10-13.
useIf: You read an older tutorial, answer an interview question about a platform, or plan an upgrade.
avoidIf: You need today's price or limit: confirm it in the live documentation, because this map is dated.

explain.md: Most of this map is about **old advice that now misleads**: a tutorial teaches Chat Completions plus reasoning plus tools, an answer says MCP needs `initialize` and a session id, or a design uses an API that has been shut down. Status values were checked on **2026-10-13**. **GA** means generally available, **Preview** has no SLA and can change, **Deprecated** still works but has an end date, and **Retired** has stopped working. When a source gave no explicit status, the row says so.

Three patterns repeat across the rows. **Parameters get stricter**: newer models reject sampling values, forced tool choice or an effort value that older models accepted. **State and protocols move toward explicit handles**: Responses and Conversations hold state on the server, and MCP dropped its implicit session. **Old surfaces end on a date**: Assistants, On Your Data, preview hosted agents and several model snapshots. Sort your own estate by the earliest end date first.

explain.title: Platform dates differ
explain.md: The same model can retire on different days on OpenAI and Azure, for example `gpt-5` on 2026-12-11 on the OpenAI API against 2027-02-09 on Azure. Always name the platform when you quote a date.

pitfalls.symptom: Chat Completions agent code fails after a model upgrade
pitfalls.cause: From GPT-5.4, tools with reasoning effort other than `none` need Responses, and a default effort of `medium` still counts
pitfalls.fix: Move the tool loop to Responses, or set effort to `none` and accept the loss of reasoning

pitfalls.symptom: An MCP client waits for a session id that never arrives
pitfalls.cause: The 2026-07-28 revision removed `initialize` and the session id
pitfalls.fix: Read the revision your server speaks and negotiate the version

pitfalls.symptom: A GA claim fails a review
pitfalls.cause: A product can be GA at the API level while a portal or a package is Preview
pitfalls.fix: State which surface you mean, for example API GA and portal Preview

scenarios.title: Agent code breaks after a model upgrade
scenarios.situation: A Chat Completions agent that calls tools ran on an older reasoning model. After moving the Azure deployment to `gpt-5.6-sol` it fails with 'Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported', although the code never sets an effort.
constraints: The model must keep reasoning for hard questions
A release is due this month
unknowns: How many tool loops depend on Chat Completions message shapes?
Is Responses available in the same Azure region?
scenarios.question: What do you do?

options.name: Keep Chat Completions and set `reasoning_effort` to `none`
options.why: The tool loop runs unchanged, which fits a tight release.
options.tradeoff: You give up reasoning, so hard questions get worse.

options.name: Move the agent loop to the Responses API
options.why: Tools with reasoning need Responses on these models, and it keeps reasoning on [[r3]] [[tr5]].
options.tradeoff: You rewrite message handling for Items and re-test the tool loop.

options.name: Keep the code and omit the effort parameter
options.why: The default effort is `medium`, so the model still reasons and the call still fails.
options.tradeoff: Omitting a parameter helps only when the default is `none`, which holds for some earlier models, so check the model page.

flips.if: Quality tests show reasoning adds nothing for this task
flips.then: Chat Completions with effort `none` is cheaper to ship.

flips.if: The code must stay portable across OpenAI-compatible vendors
flips.then: Keep Chat Completions with effort `none` behind an adapter and isolate the Responses path.

scenarios.takeaway: An unset parameter takes the model's default, and the default may be the problem.

scenarios.title: Sequence the migrations by date
scenarios.situation: On 2026-10-13 a team has a workload on `o4-mini` through the OpenAI API, a Foundry deployment of `gpt-4o` 2024-05-13, and eval dashboards on the OpenAI Evals platform.
unknowns: Can the `o4-mini` workload move to a current model without prompt rewrites?
Which eval datasets must be exported?
scenarios.question: Which work goes first?

options.name: Start with the Azure `gpt-4o` migration because it is the largest
options.why: Size is not urgency. The 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-31 dates arrive first.
options.tradeoff: Starting with the largest item is right when its date is also the earliest.

options.name: Migrate everything in one release in December
options.why: One test cycle and one rollout.
options.tradeoff: It misses the October dates and puts all the risk in one release.

options.name: Replace `o4-mini` before 2026-10-23, export Evals before 2026-10-31, then handle the Azure `gpt-4o` date of 2026-12-09
options.why: It sorts the work by the earliest end date, and the OpenAI shutdown is only 10 days away [[r2]].
options.tradeoff: The Azure work waits and has a shorter runway.

flips.if: The `o4-mini` workload already runs on another model
flips.then: The Evals export and the Azure date become the first items.
Re-sort the list, but keep the earliest published date until it is moved.

scenarios.takeaway: Sort migrations by end date per platform, not by size.

quiz.explain: These four dates anchor the API, protocol and retirement changes. The map above gives the source for each.

quiz.q: A client talks to Foundry A2A with no version header or query value. Which protocol version does it get?
quiz.explain: On the check date Foundry served preview 0.3 unless the header or the query value requested another version [[r11]]. The header and the query value must agree or the call returns 400.

quiz.q: Which changes can break existing code without any change on your side?
options: Chat Completions rejecting tools with reasoning effort other than `none` from GPT-5.4
Claude Opus 4.7 returning 400 for non-default sampling values
A model snapshot reaching its shutdown date
A new reference page in the docs
quiz.explain: A parameter rule, a sampling rule and a shutdown each change behaviour on a date. A new documentation page changes nothing at run time.

flashcards.front: What happened to the OpenAI Assistants API?
flashcards.back: Deprecation was announced on 2025-08-26 and the API was sunset on 2026-08-26. Threads map to Conversations and Runs to Responses.
The protocol became stateless: no `initialize` and no session id, multi round-trip requests replaced server push, and Tasks moved to an extension.

flashcards.front: Why can an unset reasoning effort still break tool calls?
flashcards.back: The model applies its default, often `medium`, and Chat Completions rejects tools with any effort other than `none` on newer models.

flashcards.front: Why name the platform when quoting a retirement date?
flashcards.back: The same model can retire on different dates on OpenAI and on Azure.
